About this interface

LILABI — Linguistic Landscape

An interactive map of photographed public signs. It currently covers multiple cities, with more to be added over time. Each point on the map is a sign; the three panels are the filters (left), the map (centre) and the analysis / detail panel (right). You can drag the two dividers to resize the panels.

Choosing a city

Use the City selector at the top left to switch between cities. The map re-centres and every panel updates for that city.

Filtering signs

The left sidebar lists filter groups (Language, Script, Category, Discourse, and so on). Tick any values to narrow the map to signs that carry them. Within a group you can type in its search box, re-sort the values, and switch the match mode between OR (any selected value) and AND (all of them). Counts next to each value show how many signs match. Reset all filters clears everything; Fit map to results zooms to the current selection.

Map & display options

  • Color by — colours the markers by a chosen attribute (e.g. Discourse or Language).
  • Diversity heatmap — replaces markers with a grid coloured by linguistic diversity (Simpson index) per cell; the Grid slider sets the cell size and the legend explains the colours. Click a cell to list the signs inside it.
  • Ignore proper names — excludes proper-noun language tags from diversity and language counts.
  • Show markers / district borders and the Size slider control what is drawn on the map.

The analysis panel (right side)

With nothing selected the right panel shows Selection analysis for the signs currently on the map: Composition (counts by any attribute), Co-occurrence (a cross-tab of two attributes), District comparison, and — where the data has OCR — Language size by combination and Language size by layout. It always reflects the active filters, so filtering the map also filters the analysis.

Browsing the signs

Click any marker to open that sign on the right: its photo, all metadata, and (if available) its OCR text and per-language size breakdown. The Browse photos one by one button opens a gallery you can page through with the arrows or the ← → keys. Each photo lists its sign(s) as cards.

Signs highlighted on the photographs

In the photo view each annotated sign is drawn as a coloured outline on the image. Hover a card to highlight its sign on the photo, or click the outline to jump to its card. Toggles let you show or hide Sign Highlights, and — for cities with OCR — Text and Image boxes; hovering a box shows the recognised text. Use Maximize to open a zoomable full view. For cities where photos are cropped to the sign (e.g. Helsinki), each card shows just the sign itself rather than the whole photo.

A note on the analysis

The “Language size by layout” analysis is experimental. It is produced by an automated process (OCR, per-word language detection and geometric layout estimation), so it may contain errors and should be read as an approximate guide rather than an exact measurement.
